source.title: A Blind Spot in Alignment: Quantifying Biosecurity Risks in Large Language Models
source.authors: Shu Quan; Tianfang Hao; Sitong Fang; He Geng; Jia-Yi Zhou; Bo-Yuan Chen; Kai-Le Wang; Donghai Hong; Jun-Tao Dai; Yao-Dong Yang; Jia-Ming Ji

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether safety behavior on harmful requests can be bypassed using a different intervention: adversarial prompt reformulations, measured with a sequence-level functional-risk metric. It does not test the original fine-tuning or token-position methods.
record.gate_note: The paper evaluates toxin-design requests, refusal, and predicted functional risk. It does not fine-tune target models, measure aligned-versus-base KL by response position, prefill compliant openings, use adversarial suffixes, change decoding to bypass refusal, edit safety weights, or train deeper safety. Its tested bypass condition is adversarial prompt reformulation. FHR is a computational proxy, not wet-lab-validated harm.
record.test_reason: The study measures refusal and predicted functional risk (FHR) on toxin-design prompts and tests prompt paraphrasing as a bypass. This is a different construct from V4, which is about prefilling a compliant start, suffixes or decoding changes that get past the opening tokens. Paraphrased prompts change the request itself, not the response opening. There is no fine-tuning, per-token KL, weight localization or deepening training. The reformulation results belong under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly right: refusal metrics do not predict screened functional risk, capability drives FHR, and some high-refusal models (GPT-5, GPT-5-Mini) lose protection under paraphrase while the two Claude models do not. The authors do not frame this as shallow safety alignment or as a token-position effect.
record.recipe_differences: No fine-tuning or token-level KL measurement. Tests adversarial paraphrasing and synonym/keyword changes, using FHR from compliance, plausibility, and toxicity filters rather than refusal alone or token-position measures.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies by model and paraphrase strategy. Under the four tested reformulation strategies, GPT-5 and GPT-5-Mini show large FHR increases, while Claude-3.5-Sonnet and Claude-Opus-4.6 remain at 0.0%; low-refusal models have substantial baseline FHR and often lower FHR after reformulation.

fits_no_version.finding: Paraphrasing toxin-design prompts (persona, synonym, intent concealment, keyword removal) raises FHR from 0-2% to 24-58% for GPT-5 and GPT-5-Mini, while Claude-3.5-Sonnet and Claude-Opus-4.6 stay at 0.0% (n=50 per cell). Low-refusal models stay at 18-44% with no consistent rise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal in some high-refusal models depends on toxin-specific vocabulary and fails under prompt paraphrase; other models remain robust.

fits_no_version.finding: Across 32 models, refusal rate has near-zero correlation with FHR (rho=-0.05). FHR tracks biological generation capability (Valid Rate, partial r_s=0.821). Models refusing over 90% have mean FHR 0.34% versus 15.93% for the rest.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For toxin-design prompts, refusal rate alone is a poor proxy for predicted sequence-level risk, which depends on biological generation capability.

record.problems: FHR is a computational prediction, not wet-lab validation. The OOD reformulation study uses 50 prompts per condition. The paper notes that the benchmark is primarily based on a single English prompt template and single-turn queries, with multilingual and multi-turn analyses covering only subsets.
record.rows_left_out: Did not include the full per-model Table 1 refusal-rate and FHR entries or all multilingual and defense-evaluation outcomes; these do not directly test the versions recorded here. Main matched reformulation results from Appendix O, Table 26, and aggregate refusal/FHR analyses from Appendix K are retained.

untested.parts: No per-token KL or response-position analysis.
No prefilling, adversarial suffixes or decoding changes. Only prompt paraphrase was tested, and it does not operate on the response opening.
No test of data or objective as the cause of shallowness.
No training to deepen safety. BioSafe-Guard is an input classifier, not deeper alignment.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V4 verdicts (supports, challenges, limits_scope) are withdrawn because the study never tests prefilling, suffixes or decoding changes. In Table 26 the reformulations were applied to 50 prompts and evaluated through the funnel, with the original 50 prompts as matched baseline. FHR is a computational proxy, not wet-lab validated. The 50-prompt cells are small; the Wilson intervals are given only for r18 and r25. The paper says GPT-5 and GPT-5-Mini refuse over 92% of original prompts, so the matched-baseline FHR for those two is 2% and 0%.

versions.untested_parts: No harmful-example fine-tuning intervention or measurement of safety removal after fine-tuning.
No benign-data fine-tuning intervention or measurement of its effect on harmful compliance.
No aligned-versus-base per-token KL measurement or analysis of response positions.
Tests adversarial prompt reformulation, not compliant-opening prefills, suffix attacks, decoding changes, or whether any effect operates by getting past initial response tokens.
No safety weight localization, ablation, or rank analysis.
Does not test whether data or training objectives cause safety shallowness.
No training to deepen safety or evaluation of whether such training generalizes.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: GPT-5 and GPT-5-Mini under adversarial prompt reformulations
reader_labels.reason: FHR rises substantially from matched original-prompt values for both high-refusal models; GPT-5 reaches 50.0–52.0% in two strategies and GPT-5-Mini reaches 58.0% under keyword removal (r17–r20, r22–r25).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Claude-3.5-Sonnet and Claude-Opus-4.6 under the four tested reformulation strategies
reader_labels.reason: The authors report FHR = 0.0% for both models across all strategies, so the tested prompt attacks do not bypass their protection in this evaluation (r26–r33).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Gemini-3-Flash, Gemini-3.1-Pro, and GPT-OSS-120B under the tested reformulations
reader_labels.reason: These models already have substantial FHR on the original prompts; reformulations often lower rather than raise FHR, so the results do not show that reformulation newly defeats an effective refusal in these models (r01–r15).
